::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## Takeaways
- **Every play already has a written description**, e.g. "Pullup Jump Shot", "Cutting Dunk Shot", "(X assists)",
  "X blocks Y's shot". Treating each player-season's plays as a document gives a text layer with no scraping.
- **Topics found from text alone match recognizable roles:** rim finishers, post scorers, pull-up shooters and
  spot-up shooters.
- **Text groups partly agree with the stat archetypes** (ARI 0.23 NBA,
  0.25 WNBA). The text sees *how* players score and pass; the stat model also sees
  usage, rebounding rates and defense.
- **Zero-shot labels** (from written role descriptions, checked against the player's position) agree with the stat
  archetypes 36% of the time (chance is about 17%), and with the blind hand labels
  42% of the time, close to the stat archetypes' 48%.
:::

:::


## How it works

- **Documents:** one per player-season (NBA 2017-18 onward and WNBA 2019 onward, where the play text names shot
  types; at least 500 minutes).
- **Tokens:**
  - **Shot type** (e.g. *pullup jump shot three*). A made shot and a missed shot of the same type are the **same
    token**, weighted: each attempt counts once and each make counts again. A movement shooter who takes and makes
    many threes scores high on *jump shot three*; a defender who takes them and misses still shows the shot, with less weight.
  - **Playmaking:** each assist records what the pass set up: *assist to a three*, *to the rim* or *to the mid-range*.
  - **Defense and possession:** blocks, steals, rebounds, and all turnover types merged into one *turnover* token.
- **Preprocessing:** lower-casing, punctuation stripped, one token per play type, administrative events (substitutions,
  timeouts) removed, play types used by fewer than 20 players dropped.
- **TF-IDF:** term frequency (dampened) times inverse document frequency, so a rare play like an *alley-oop dunk* weighs
  more than a common *defensive rebound*.
- **Position cross-check:** the distinctive plays of each archetype are measured against players **at the same
  listed position**; text clustering uses the text plus the player's position; a zero-shot label must fit the position
  (a center can't be labeled a secondary guard).
- **Embeddings:** LSA, a 50-dimension compression of TF-IDF that places related play types together (no download needed).
- **Topic model:** non-negative matrix factorization, 8 topics. **Text clustering:** K-Means (k = 6).
- **Zero-shot labeling:** each archetype was described in words before results were seen; each player gets the most
  similar description that fits their position. The hand labels were only used to score the result.

## Plays that set each archetype apart

The plays most over-represented in each archetype compared with players **at the same position**, split into shots and
playmaking & defense, so common but defining actions like passing aren't crowded out by rare shot types.


**NBA**

| archetype               | shots                                                                                                 | playmaking & defense                               |
|:------------------------|:------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:---------------------------------------------------|
| Connector forward       | cutting dunk shot, dunk shot, tip dunk shot, tip shot                                                 | offensive rebound, block, defensive rebound        |
| Hub big / point forward | turnaround fade away jump shot, turnaround hook shot, turnaround bank jump shot, hook turnaround bank | (nothing above same-position players)              |
| On-ball creator         | pullup bank jump shot, step back jump shot, fade away jump shot, driving jump shot bank               | assist rim, assist mid, assist three, turnover     |
| Rim-running big         | alley oop dunk shot, dunk shot, putback dunk shot, hook shot                                          | offensive rebound, block                           |
| Secondary guard         | pullup jump shot three, pullup jump shot, step back jump shot, running pullup jump shot               | assist rim, assist mid, assist three, turnover     |
| Spot-up 3-and-D wing    | jump shot three, running jump shot three, shooting foul, personal foul                                | defensive rebound, steal, offensive rebound, block |


**WNBA**

| archetype               | shots                                                                                                  | playmaking & defense                                      |
|:------------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:----------------------------------------------------------|
| Connector forward       | layup shot putback, cutting layup shot, layup shot, turnaround jump shot                               | offensive rebound, block, defensive rebound, steal        |
| Hub big / point forward | turnaround bank jump shot, turnaround fade away jump shot, fade away jump shot, step back jump shot    | (nothing above same-position players)                     |
| On-ball creator         | pullup jump shot three, running pullup jump shot, step back jump shot three, driving finger roll layup | assist rim, assist three, assist mid, turnover            |
| Rim-running big         | turnaround hook shot, hook shot, layup shot putback, tip shot                                          | block, offensive rebound, defensive rebound, turnover     |
| Secondary guard         | pullup jump shot three, running pullup jump shot, pullup jump shot, step back jump shot three          | assist mid, assist rim, assist three, turnover            |
| Spot-up 3-and-D wing    | jump shot three, running jump shot three, shooting foul, personal foul                                 | defensive rebound, steal, offensive rebound, assist three |


**What this shows:** creators and secondary guards stand out for pull-ups, step-backs and assists of every kind; spot-up 3-and-D wings for catch-and-shoot threes, steals and rebounds; rim-running bigs for dunks, putbacks and blocks. One finding to note: **hub bigs / point forwards do not pass more than other forwards and centers** in this data. The group is defined more by post scoring (turnaround hooks and fades) than by playmaking, so its true point-forward passers (Jokić-type players) are better identified by their sub-type and assist rates than by the group name.

| WNBA     | text clustering (K-Means on LSA, k=6)                           |  691 | 0.255 | 0.361 |                              |                           |

**What this shows:** each row is a group the text found on its own; the numbers are how many player-seasons of each stat archetype landed in it. Rows dominated by one column (e.g. the pull-up row by creators and secondary guards) mean the text and the stats agree; spread-out rows are roles the text alone can't separate.



## Reputation text (next step)

How teams are *described* (offense-first, defense-first) can be compared with how they *played*. The program
`scripts/fetch_team_text.py` downloads team-season articles from Wikipedia's official API (rate-limited, cached
locally, not republished), and `src/step4_reputation.py` scores offense/defense emphasis and sentiment with TF-IDF
and word lists, then compares them with measured team identity. It has to run on a computer that can reach Wikipedia.
